title: tooling: turbo 2.11.5 writes a managed block into AGENTS.md in every agent worktree; opt out with "agentGuidance": false in turbo.json
body:
Filing-gate class: ① a defect with a named site and a measured reproduction. It is a regression from today's #21024 landing.
Routing: the maintainer direct-dispatch channel (`session_018gA1pE6eJtwHhqx72G8U9X`; 「相关卡片你使用项目经理技能派发处理」). It is fallout of #21024, which that ruling authorized. Routed to `domain:devx` / `area:devpath`; triage grades the priority.
Acting reader: the dispatching seat's `os-dev`, for one line in the root `turbo.json`.
Dedup: I listed objectstack's issues over REST (open, plus the most recently updated closed) and grepped them for `agentGuidance`, `turborepo-agent-rules` and `turbo 2.11`. 0 hits. There is no card for this.

## Measured

- **When it started:** #21024 landed `turbo` 2.11.5 on `main` at 2026-10-01T08:59Z. It had been 2.10.10. The lockfile now holds `turbo@2.11.5`.
- **What turbo does:** `turbo` 2.11's root option `agentGuidance` defaults to `true`. Its bundled `docs/reference/configuration.mdx` says: "When an AI coding agent is detected, `turbo` maintains a managed block in the repository-root `AGENTS.md`… refreshed before repository-scoped commands."
- **Observed at 09:5xZ:** in the worktree of the in-flight #21094 dev, `git diff -- AGENTS.md` shows an 11-line uncommitted append, `<!-- BEGIN:turborepo-agent-rules -->` … `<!-- END:turborepo-agent-rules -->`. The dev never edited `AGENTS.md`.
- **Why it matters:**
  - The block tells agents to "keep the block committed with your work".
  - `AGENTS.md` is a governed surface. Any dev that obeys turns its PR into a human-approval PR, and the queue guard holds it there.
  - Every seat's dev hits this on its first `turbo` call.
- **Reach at filing:** none of objectstack's 11 open PRs touches `AGENTS.md` yet. objectui is unaffected (`turbo@2.10.9`).

## What to do

1. Add `"agentGuidance": false` to the root `turbo.json`. That is the opt-out the bundled docs name, and it is a root-only option.
2. Acceptance: a `turbo` run under an agent leaves `AGENTS.md` unchanged. Show `git diff --exit-code -- AGENTS.md` after a repository-scoped `turbo` command, with a positive control first: the same command without the opt-out does write the block.
3. Per the docs, the opt-out does not remove a block already written. Worktrees that already carry it restore with `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree AGENTS.md`. ⛔ Never commit the block.
4. Changeset: `turbo.json` publishes nothing, so `skip-changeset`.
